research_analysis.exact_observed_hook: "I have no idea what I'm doing with my life."
research_analysis.visual_hook: Close-up selfie of a young man by an alpine lake with the Matterhorn behind him. Centered white text reads "i have no idea".
research_analysis.narrative_structure: Confession cold open (0-2s). Seven rapid "I want X, but I want Y" pairs, one every 2 to 3 seconds (2-22s). One-word pivot, "Wait." (22s). A long sentence that restates the list as one impossible demand (23-33s). Then a 35-second sincere reframe about choosing. 26 shots, word-by-word lowercase captions, acoustic music, no CTA.
research_analysis.viral_mechanism: Each pair is a separate recognition test. A viewer only needs to see themselves in one pair to keep watching, and the pairs arrive faster than they can scroll. The pivot word resets attention at the 30% mark.
research_analysis.observed_evidence: 1.6M views against a 22.5K median (69.4x) on a 77K account. 73 seconds long, so the views were earned with a long video, which implies the list section held people. The first 22 seconds contain 7 pairs and 10 shots. No speech-free section; captions cover every word.
research_analysis.performance_hypothesis: Hypothesis: viewers send it to one specific friend with "this is literally us" because a pair names a tension they have said out loud. The comment behaviour is quoting the pair that hit. The sincere back half is where drop-off is likely, which is why the adaptation cuts it.
research_analysis.why_this_format_fits_alex: His audit shows no working narrative lifestyle video yet, and his feed never says he is 23 or what he is building. The contradiction list lets him state his real facts (agency, Florida move, the Lexus, months of not posting, the 100K goal) as jokes rather than as a flex. It is spoken, so it uses the delivery that drove comments on the 2.8M client skit.
research_analysis.originality_changes: Borrowed: confession opener, the "I want X but Y" list rhythm, the one-word pivot, the restated impossible demand. New: every pair is written from his own life, the tone is comic instead of earnest, the footage is his ordinary day instead of travel b-roll, the sincere 35-second reframe is replaced by a 6-second decision tied to his public goal, and the runtime drops from 73s to 38s.

alex_adaptation.concept: Alex lists the contradictions of being 23 and running a business, each one specific to him, then resolves it by picking exactly one thing: posting every day until 100K.
alex_adaptation.target_audience: People 18 to 30 who are building something or want to, and feel pulled in six directions.
alex_adaptation.first_frame: Tight selfie, Alex in his car in a parking lot, engine off, staring just past the lens like he has been sitting there a while. Text: "i'm 23 and i want things that cancel each other out".
alex_adaptation.first_spoken_line: I'm twenty-three and everything I want cancels out something else I want.

production.location: His car (parked), his desk, his bedroom at night, one outdoor spot near home, a grocery run.
production.wardrobe: Whatever he actually wears on a normal workday. One outfit for car and desk, a different T-shirt for the night shot.
shot_list: Car selfie: opening line, "Wait.", finger-count line, closing line and drive-off (film all four in one sitting)
Desk wide: looking for a boss
Pan from laptop to sunny window
Wide: filming himself on tripod, hiding from a passer-by
Insert: grocery bag wearing a seatbelt
Screen recording: his grid scrolling and stopping
b_roll: Extra 2-second inserts of the palm trees, the tripod legs, and the steering wheel badge for cutaways if a line is re-recorded
production.editor_instructions: Record the six VO pairs as clean audio in the parked car, same sitting as the selfie lines, so the room tone matches. Lowercase captions, max two lines, centered at 60% height. One pair per 3 to 4 seconds, never longer. Kill the music entirely from "Wait." until "So I picked one." That silence is the retention reset. No zoom transitions, hard cuts only.

variants_to_test: Alternate hook: "Being 23 is wanting two opposite things, eleven times a day."
Alternate payoff: the silent tripod ending with "day 1."
testing.promotion_decision: Brand fit 3. Promote at 48h if views are at least 3x the trailing median and follows per 1,000 reached is in the top quartile; if follows are high under 6K views, re-film only the first 3 seconds with the alternate hooks.
follow_up_variations_if_successful: Same list structure, subject: running an agency ("I want clients who trust me. I want to be left alone by clients.")
Same list, subject: moving to a new state alone at 23

creative_confidence.score_type: Subjective production-priority score, not predicted viral probability
creative_confidence.rationale: The list section is the part of the reference that the data most plausibly rewards, and every pair here is anchored to a stated fact about Alex. It tells a non-follower his age, his business, his move and his goal in 38 seconds, which none of his recent Reels do. It is spoken and 38 seconds, which is outside his proven silent sub-10-second zone, so reach is less certain than conversion.
uncertainties: The sport-mode and beach lines are jokes built on real facts (the Lexus, Florida). Alex should cut any pair that is not true for him.
"I don't want anyone from high school to see me trying" must be something he actually feels or it will read as borrowed.
Nine setups make this one of the slower videos to shoot.
